subject.title: RFC: Standard Hosting Profiles and Ready Check

question: Should OpenClaw core own named hosting profiles and make their topology predicates authoritative readiness conditions?
rationale: The RFC creates a permanent configuration surface, support promise, and availability contract; neither current main nor repository discussion establishes that product boundary, so automation cannot choose it safely.

options.title: Approve the readiness foundation only
options.body: Accept the canonical condition model and default local projection first, while deferring non-local profiles and blocking release gates until live compatibility evidence exists.

options.title: Approve the full profile roadmap
options.body: Adopt all four profiles, selection precedence, fail-closed predicates, and package-release conformance as one core roadmap.

options.title: Keep topology checks downstream
options.body: Decline named profiles in core and retain deployment-shape validation in hosts or optional tooling.

recommendation.title: Approve the readiness foundation only
recommendation.body: Accept the canonical condition model and default local projection first, while deferring non-local profiles and blocking release gates until live compatibility evidence exists.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent repository-level merge history and active adjacent OpenClaw runtime work make this the strongest available product-decision routing signal.
